correctness.rationale: Read entire RESULT.md at frozen blob 7b607ba36acbcb6bd34ca311f4efa52b3270ba29. Required weight-two de Bruijn edges form disjoint directed rotation necklace circuits, each with one incoming and outgoing required edge at every incident (k-1)-word. Adding the cycle induced by 10^(k-2) has length k-1 and passes through all single-marker (k-1)-words; each required necklace touches one, hence the union is balanced and connected and Eulerian. For the lower bound, subtract one copy of each mandatory edge. Any fewer than k-1 additional edges decompose into short periodic circuits. A short circuit meeting the adjacent-pair necklace cannot meet another weight-two necklace; Fine–Wilf forces any two meeting short circuits to have identical primitive vertex support. Thus short extras cannot connect the required distinct necklaces. Fresh independent Euler constructions checked literal windows for k=4..17; exhaustive shorter cyclic binary words were checked at k=4,5. These are finite corroborations of the all-k Fine–Wilf proof.
